name: Temporary Residence -- Serbian Origin

qualifying_event.description: A foreign national who can document blood or adoptive kinship, in a direct line, with an ancestor who was a citizen of the Republic of Serbia (or of a predecessor state) may obtain temporary residence on this basis, without needing an independent economic or family-sponsorship ground.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Public civil records establishing the lineage (birth/citizenship records of the ancestor), or, where public records are unavailable, church records -- the government's own guidance names a baptism record issued by the Serbian Orthodox Church as an acceptable form of documentary evidence of Serbian heritage.

requirements.blocker_text: Must document blood or adoptive kinship, in a direct line, with an ancestor who was a citizen of the Republic of Serbia or of a predecessor state (e.g. the Kingdom of Serbia, the Kingdom of Yugoslavia, or the SFRY), via public records or, where unavailable, church records including Serbian Orthodox Church baptism records.

evidence_required.document: Public civil/citizenship records documenting the ancestor's lineage
Church records (e.g. Serbian Orthodox Church baptism record), where public records are unavailable

sources.title: Serbian Ministry of Interior (MUP) -- 'Serbian origin' temporary residence ground: proof of direct-line blood or adoptive kinship with a citizen ancestor (current or predecessor state), evidenced by public records or church records including Serbian Orthodox Church baptism records

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Serbia). pr_after_months and citizenship_after_months modeled 0 (not a fixed wait) because MUP's own permanent-residence page (see rs_permanent_residence.json) explicitly exempts persons 'originating from or of Serbian descent' from the general 3-year continuous-residence requirement -- and the Law on Citizenship separately grants persons of Serbian origin (see rs_citizenship_serbian_origin.json, Article 23) a direct citizenship-admission route without needing residence in Serbia at all, so this residence permit is best understood as one of several parallel doors rather than a fixed-duration prerequisite step. work_rights modeled 'full' since no employer/activity restriction was described for this ground, unlike the employment- and business-based grounds. The requirement's evidentiary reliance on Serbian Orthodox Church baptism records (a specific, named religious institution) as government-accepted proof of ethnic/national heritage is modeled and disclosed exactly as MUP states it, since it is a factual feature of the eligibility criteria rather than an editorial choice.
